Definition: probably by variation for G3425; with difficulty:--hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work.
BiblicalUsage: Molis means hardly, scarcely, with difficulty — the crowd at Lystra is hardly restrained from sacrificing to Paul and Barnabas, the ship sails slowly and with difficulty toward Cnidus, and Paul says scarcely for a righteous man will one die.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word keeps me honest about how hard things are: hardly restrained, hardly sailing, hardly dying for another — and grace does it anyway.
